name: machine_society_evaluation_taxonomy
description: A compact, evolving taxonomy for coding how AI participants evaluate intelligence in machine-society experiments. Tags are intentionally behavioral and observable rather than claims about internal state.
basis: Human cognitive assessment families: verbal comprehension, fluid reasoning, quantitative reasoning, working memory, processing speed, visual-spatial reasoning, crystallized knowledge, and social judgment.
Educational and admissions assessment families: reading comprehension, analytical writing, quantitative reasoning, scientific reasoning, philosophy, and argument critique.

AI evaluation families: knowledge QA, math/STEM reasoning, code generation and repair, long-context retrieval, instruction following, tool use, robustness, safety, multilinguality, multimodal perception, and agentic task completion.

Observed pilot questions: liar/paradox puzzles, metaphor/tower reframing, market scenario planning, pattern/music analogy probes, source-verification probes, dimensional-analysis probes, recursive self-bias probes, uncertainty updates, and evaluator-quality judgments.

tags.label: Criteria Setting
tags.description: Defines, debates, or revises what intelligence should mean in the experiment.

tags.label: Direct Task Probe
tags.description: Uses a concrete question, puzzle, domain task, or mini-test to elicit capability evidence.

tags.label: Adaptive Follow-Up
tags.description: Changes the next probe in response to a participant's previous answer, weakness, or uncertainty.

tags.label: Edge-Case Testing
tags.description: Stress-tests a proposal by searching for failure modes, contradictions, edge cases, or boundary conditions.

tags.label: Transfer Test
tags.description: Tests whether a participant can transfer structure across domains, analogies, metaphors, or unfamiliar contexts.

tags.label: Self-Assessment
tags.description: Reflects on the participant's own performance, uncertainty, weaknesses, or relative standing.

tags.label: Evaluator Evaluation
tags.description: Treats the quality of questions, probes, rankings, or evaluation methods as evidence of intelligence.

tags.label: Uncertainty Calibration
tags.description: Expresses confidence, ambiguity, evidence limits, probabilities, or conditions that would change the judgment.

tags.label: Strategic Signaling
tags.description: Attempts to persuade, claim status, frame the contest, or signal superior capability rather than only demonstrate it.

tags.label: Performative Evasion
tags.description: Uses impressive framing, generic abstraction, or process talk while avoiding the demanded substantive answer.

tags.label: Deception Or Gaming
tags.description: Attempts to bluff, manipulate criteria, mislead others, or game the evaluation.

tags.label: Consensus Formation
tags.description: Defers to another participant, adopts a shared ranking, or shifts toward group consensus.

question_types.label: Verbal Abstraction
question_types.description: Asks for similarities, definitions, analogies, conceptual distinctions, or abstract verbal relationships.

question_types.label: Language Induction
question_types.description: Infers grammar, morphology, syntax, or meaning rules from examples in an unfamiliar or constructed language.

question_types.label: Knowledge Recall
question_types.description: Tests acquired factual, cultural, scientific, historical, or domain-specific knowledge.

question_types.label: Fluid Reasoning
question_types.description: Uses unfamiliar rules, patterns, matrix-like relations, hidden structure, or novel problem solving.

question_types.label: Logic And Consistency
question_types.description: Tests formal consistency, contradictions, paradoxes, truth conditions, or hidden assumptions.

question_types.label: Math Reasoning
question_types.description: Asks for arithmetic, algebra, probability, combinatorics, optimization, formal proof, or quantitative modeling.

question_types.label: Units And Dimensions
question_types.description: Tests unit analysis, dimensional consistency, equation repair, or whether a quantitative model has coherent physical units.

question_types.label: Scientific Reasoning
question_types.description: Tests causal models, experimental design, hypothesis evaluation, physics/biology/chemistry reasoning, or evidence interpretation.

question_types.label: Source Verification
question_types.description: Tests citation discipline, source reliability, fact-checking plans, retraction under uncertainty, or empirical-claim verification.

question_types.label: Coding
question_types.description: Asks for code, algorithms, debugging, complexity analysis, data structures, or program synthesis.

question_types.label: Computer Systems
question_types.description: Tests distributed protocols, concurrency, transactions, consistency, crash recovery, or systems architecture.

question_types.label: Software Engineering
question_types.description: Requires modifying a codebase, diagnosing failures, using tests, planning edits, or completing a realistic engineering task.

question_types.label: State Tracking
question_types.description: Tests retention, manipulation, ordering, bookkeeping, or tracking entities across turns.

question_types.label: Speed And Efficiency
question_types.description: Tests fast, concise, or resource-constrained performance under time, token, or complexity limits.

question_types.label: Spatial And Visual Reasoning
question_types.description: Uses visual patterns, diagrams, spatial transformations, scene understanding, or perceptual detail.

question_types.label: Reading And Argument
question_types.description: Asks for close reading, summarization, inference from text, argument evaluation, or critique of claims.

question_types.label: Creative Generation
question_types.description: Elicits original ideas, metaphors, hypotheses, stories, alternative uses, or multiple plausible solutions.

question_types.label: Planning And Strategy
question_types.description: Asks for goal-directed plans, tradeoffs, scenario analysis, policy choices, or strategic prioritization.

question_types.label: Social And Moral Judgment
question_types.description: Tests social reasoning, norms, ethical tradeoffs, interpersonal judgment, or real-world common sense.

question_types.label: Philosophical Analysis
question_types.description: Tests conceptual analysis, ontology, epistemology, normative foundations, thought experiments, or the coherence of abstract claims.

question_types.label: Calibration
question_types.description: Asks the respondent to estimate confidence, identify uncertainty, assess its own limits, or update beliefs.

question_types.label: Recursive Self-Critique
question_types.description: Asks about hidden assumptions, bias in one's own reasoning, higher-order uncertainty, or correction of correction methods.

question_types.label: Long-Context Synthesis
question_types.description: Requires finding, integrating, or comparing information across long transcripts, documents, or many turns.

question_types.label: Instruction Following
question_types.description: Tests adherence to constraints, output format, schemas, word limits, or exact instructions.

question_types.label: Robustness
question_types.description: Tests resistance to misleading premises, adversarial framing, unsafe requests, manipulation, or distribution shift.

question_types.label: Multilingual And Cultural Reasoning
question_types.description: Tests language transfer, translation, cross-lingual understanding, or cultural context.

question_types.label: Tool Use
question_types.description: Requires choosing or using tools, APIs, search, execution, verification, or environment interaction.
